quick_facts.label: What the job is
quick_facts.value: Market research analysts research conditions in local, regional, national or online markets, and gather information to estimate the potential sales of a product or service or to plan a marketing campaign.

quick_facts.label: Other names for it
quick_facts.value: Job titles O*NET reports for this occupation (Market Research Analysts and Marketing Specialists) include Market Research Analyst, Market Analyst, Market Research Specialist and Business Development Specialist.

quick_facts.label: Typical preparation
quick_facts.value: O*NET places this occupation in Job Zone Four (considerable preparation needed): most of these occupations require a four-year bachelor's degree, but some do not.

sections.heading: What a market research analyst does
paragraphs: Market research analysts research conditions in local, regional, national or online markets, and gather information to estimate the potential sales of a product or service or to plan a marketing campaign.

The tasks below are taken from the O*NET profile for Market Research Analysts and Marketing Specialists. O*NET is the US Department of Labor's occupation database, so this describes the job as it is profiled in the United States; titles and duties in Indian companies can differ.
bullets: Collect and analyse data on customer demographics, preferences, needs and buying habits.
Gather data on competitors and analyse their prices, sales and marketing methods.
Design and evaluate ways of collecting data, such as surveys and opinion polls.
Prepare reports that show findings in charts and plain written text.

sections.heading: How people get into this job
paragraphs: O*NET places this occupation in Job Zone Four (considerable preparation needed): most of these occupations require a four-year bachelor's degree, but some do not.
O*NET is the US Department of Labor's occupation database, so this describes the job as it is profiled in the United States; titles and duties in Indian companies can differ.
bullets: Common routes into this job on the Career Tree map: BBA (Bachelor of Business Administration); MBA (Master of Business Administration).
Less common routes on the map: BA (Bachelor of Arts); M.Sc. in Economics.
